stories.title: Japanese firm sells profitable Ethereum, Solana and XRP stakes to preserve $121M Bitcoin holdings
stories.summary: A Japanese company that had booked gains on its Ethereum, Solana, and XRP positions sold those holdings, choosing instead to keep its Bitcoin reserves intact. The company's Bitcoin holdings are valued at roughly $121 million. The move signals a preference for concentrating treasury exposure in Bitcoin over other digital assets.
stories.whyItMatters: It's another data point in the trend of corporate treasuries treating Bitcoin as the preferred long-term reserve asset over other cryptocurrencies.
whatToWatch: Whether other corporate holders follow with similar altcoin-to-Bitcoin rebalancing
Any disclosure of the company's future Bitcoin accumulation plans
questions: What prompted the sale of the altcoin positions specifically now?
Does the company plan to redeploy proceeds into more Bitcoin?

sources.title: This Japanese company made money on Ethereum, Solana, and XRP, but sold them anyway to keep its $121 million Bitcoin holdings

stories.title: CFTC moves to dismiss CME's lawsuit over crypto perpetual futures
stories.summary: The Commodity Futures Trading Commission has filed to dismiss a lawsuit brought by CME Group concerning crypto perpetual futures. Both Cointelegraph and Decrypt reported the filing, with Decrypt noting the agency is asking a judge to throw out the case. Details of CME's original claims and the CFTC's stated grounds for dismissal were not specified in the reports.
stories.whyItMatters: The dispute touches on how US regulators and established exchanges will divide oversight of perpetual futures, a derivative product central to crypto trading volume.
whatToWatch: The judge's ruling on the CFTC's dismissal request
Any response or appeal from CME Group
questions: What specific legal grounds is the CFTC citing for dismissal?
What was CME originally seeking from the lawsuit?

stories.title: Bitcoin ETFs rebound as Ethereum and XRP ETF inflow streaks end
stories.summary: US spot Bitcoin ETFs saw renewed inflows, reversing recent weakness, while Ethereum and XRP ETFs saw their multi-day inflow streaks come to a halt. The shift suggests a rotation in investor demand back toward Bitcoin-focused funds. No specific dollar figures were provided in the source report.
stories.whyItMatters: ETF flow trends are a key gauge of institutional appetite and can signal which assets are attracting fresh capital versus profit-taking.
whatToWatch: Whether Bitcoin ETF inflows continue in coming sessions
Whether Ethereum and XRP ETFs resume inflows or see outflows next
questions: What drove the reversal in relative demand between Bitcoin and altcoin ETFs?

stories.title: Bitcoin demand signals turn negative as price struggles to hold $77K
stories.summary: On-chain demand indicators for Bitcoin have turned negative even as the price struggles to hold above $77,000, according to Cointelegraph. A separate CryptoSlate analysis notes that a breakout toward $80,000 would still need to absorb roughly $47 billion of profitable supply currently held by investors. Together the reports point to a market caught between weakening near-term demand and a large pool of holders sitting on gains who could sell into any rally.
stories.whyItMatters: Weakening demand alongside a large overhang of profitable supply is a classic setup for continued price chop, which matters for anyone timing entries or exits.
whatToWatch: Whether apparent demand metrics turn positive again
Whether price can clear $80,000 without triggering heavy profit-taking
questions: What is driving the drop in apparent demand specifically?
How much of the $47 billion in profitable supply is likely to be sold near $80K?

sources.title: Bitcoin’s next $80,000 breakout has $47 billion more profitable supply to absorb
Bitcoin’s apparent demand turns negative as price struggles with $77K

stories.title: Bitcoin whipsaws around $77,000 as ETF investors mirror the volatility
stories.summary: Bitcoin has been trading in a choppy range around $77,000, and spot ETF investors appear to be reacting with similarly volatile flow patterns, per CryptoSlate. The report frames both price action and fund flows as indecisive rather than trending in either direction.
stories.whyItMatters: Choppy price action paired with erratic ETF flows suggests institutional investors are as uncertain about direction as retail traders.
whatToWatch: Whether Bitcoin breaks decisively out of the $77,000 range
ETF flow data over the coming days for signs of a clearer trend
questions: What catalyst, if any, would resolve the current indecision?

sources.title: Bitcoin keeps whipsawing around $77,000, and ETF investors are doing the same

stories.title: Coldcard hacker converts stolen Bitcoin into ETH via THORChain
stories.summary: An attacker behind a theft involving Coldcard hardware wallets has swapped the stolen Bitcoin for Ethereum using the cross-chain protocol THORChain, according to Cointelegraph. The report does not specify the total amount stolen or how the original theft occurred.
stories.whyItMatters: Cross-chain swap protocols like THORChain remain a preferred laundering route for stolen crypto, complicating recovery efforts and tracing.
whatToWatch: Whether investigators or Coldcard can trace the converted funds further
Any official statement from Coldcard on the scope of the breach
questions: How was the Bitcoin originally stolen from Coldcard users?
How much total value was involved in the theft?

stories.title: Mantle integrates Paxos' USDG stablecoin, joins Global Dollar Network
stories.summary: Mantle has added Paxos' USDG stablecoin to its network and joined the Global Dollar Network, according to Cointelegraph. The move expands the set of blockchains supporting USDG as part of the Paxos-backed stablecoin alliance.
stories.whyItMatters: Stablecoin distribution across more chains widens USDG's reach and is part of the broader competition among dollar-pegged tokens for liquidity and network effects.
whatToWatch: Adoption metrics for USDG on Mantle following integration
Other networks that may join the Global Dollar Network
questions: How does this integration affect USDG's total circulating supply and liquidity?

stories.title: Dubai's VARA and Securitize sign MoU on tokenization
stories.summary: Dubai's Virtual Assets Regulatory Authority (VARA) and tokenization firm Securitize have signed a memorandum of understanding aimed at advancing tokenization innovation in the emirate, per Cointelegraph. The agreement's specific commitments or timelines were not detailed in the report.
stories.whyItMatters: It signals continued regulatory engagement between a major crypto hub and real-world-asset tokenization firms, an area regulators globally are still working out how to oversee.
whatToWatch: Concrete tokenization projects or pilots to emerge from the MoU
Follow-on regulatory guidance from VARA on tokenized assets
questions: What specific tokenization activities will the MoU actually enable or regulate?

stories.title: Ether and XRP ETF inflow streaks end as Bitcoin funds rebound
stories.summary: Ethereum and XRP spot ETFs saw their recent runs of consecutive daily inflows come to an end, while Bitcoin ETFs rebounded with renewed inflows, according to Cointelegraph. The report frames this as a shift in relative institutional demand across the three assets' fund products.
stories.whyItMatters: ETF flow reversals across assets can indicate rotating institutional sentiment and are closely watched as a proxy for where large investors see near-term value.
whatToWatch: Whether Ethereum and XRP ETFs return to net inflows
Continuation of the Bitcoin ETF rebound in coming sessions
questions: What specifically triggered the end of the Ether and XRP inflow streaks?

stories.title: Bitcoin reclaims $80K as dollar index falls amid suspected yen intervention
stories.summary: Bitcoin climbed back above $80,000 as the US Dollar Index (DXY) declined, a move Cointelegraph links to ongoing suspected intervention in the yen. The report ties Bitcoin's bounce to broader currency market dynamics rather than crypto-specific news.
stories.whyItMatters: Bitcoin's sensitivity to dollar strength and currency-market intervention shows how macro forces continue to drive crypto price action alongside sector-specific catalysts.
whatToWatch: Further confirmation or denial of yen intervention by Japanese authorities
Whether Bitcoin holds above $80,000 or reverses with DXY
questions: Is the suspected yen intervention confirmed by Japanese officials?
How durable is the correlation between DXY moves and Bitcoin's price here?

stories.title: Bitcoin jumps as Fed signals rate pause, liquidating $415M in short positions
stories.summary: Bitcoin rallied after the Federal Reserve signaled a pause in rate moves, according to Decrypt, triggering roughly $415 million in liquidations of short positions across crypto derivatives markets. The report ties the price pump directly to the Fed signal rather than crypto-specific developments.
stories.whyItMatters: Bitcoin's reaction to Fed policy signals underscores how tightly correlated crypto has become with broader monetary policy expectations.
whatToWatch: The Fed's next policy meeting and statements for confirmation of a pause
Whether the rally holds or short covering was the primary driver
questions: How much of the price move was driven by the forced short liquidations versus genuine new buying?

stories.title: Bitcoin miner abandons mining site for AI deal potentially worth over $1.2 billion
stories.summary: A Bitcoin mining company is giving up one of its mining sites in favor of a deal tied to AI infrastructure that could be worth more than $1.2 billion, according to Decrypt. The report frames this as part of a broader trend of miners pivoting facilities toward AI compute demand.
stories.whyItMatters: It's another sign that Bitcoin miners are increasingly repurposing power and infrastructure for AI workloads, which can affect network hashrate and miner economics.
whatToWatch: Finalization and terms of the AI deal
Whether other miners announce similar site conversions
questions: What happens to the site's existing mining hardware and hashrate contribution?
What are the actual terms and milestones behind the $1.2 billion figure?
